definition: Mechanisms, rules, or filters put in place around an AI system to constrain its behavior and prevent harmful, incorrect, or off-policy outputs.
details: Guardrails can operate at multiple levels, including input filtering, output filtering, and behavioral constraints built into the model itself through training, and are a common component of production LLM applications.
story: Picture a parachute packed by a second pair of hands: nobody plans to need it, but everyone is glad it was checked. Here is the short version: Mechanisms, rules, or filters put in place around an AI system to constrain its behavior and prevent harmful, incorrect, or off-policy outputs. The part that makes it sing: Guardrails can operate at multiple levels, including input filtering, output filtering, and behavioral constraints built into the model itself through training, and are a common component of production LLM applications. Caution is not the enemy of progress — it is the reason progress gets to keep going. And that is Guardrails — the reason we can move fast without breaking things, or people.
